the development of a CFD methodology for GDI engines, and its validation using experimental optical engine data.
the development of an innovative methodology to simulate the charge formation process of modern Gasesoline Direct Injection engines.
the development of a comprehensive Computational Fluid Dynamics methodology for the simulation and optimization of the charge formation in spark ignited engines.

this work has shown that the CFD simulations of the charge motion in the cylinder can be used to assess the engine performance and to drive and support a GDI engine development process.

the CFD methodology proposed in this work is a valuable tool for the engine development, capable to reproduce the complex phenomena of spray atomization and charge motion in cylinder, and to provide useful information to support the engine calibration process.
this thesis represents the first attempt to propose a CFD methodology for GDI engines, capable to be used as a tool to support and to guide the engine development process.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we developed a methodology capable to reproduce the charge formation process for spark ignited engines.

the proposed methodology allows to perform CFD simulations of the charge formation in GDI engine in a reduced amount of time, with a reduced amount of parameters and with a high level of reliability, allowing to use CFD in the engine development process to address some crucial aspects, such as the wall impingements and the mixture quality.

we developed a CFD methodology capable to correctly simulate the charge formation process and the mixture quality for different spark ignited engines, using a reduced number of calibration parameters.
The main takeaway from our work is that
CFD simulations of the charge formation in cylinder can provide useful information to support and drive the development of GDI engines.
the proposed methodology is a valid tool for the engine development, allowing to reproduce the main phenomena involved in the charge formation and to support the engine calibration process.
the CFD simulation of GDI engines, when correctly set, is capable to reproduce the experimental data with a very good agreement.
